heading_en: Minimum Requirements for the Top-Down Approach, etc.
summary_ja: トップ・ダウン・アプローチ等を用いる場合の五つの要件と各基準の内容を定める。
summary_en: Sets five requirements for top-down estimation and purchased retail exposures (legal framework, monitoring, workout, collateral and credit limit controls, compliance) and defines each standard.
paragraphs: Where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach estimates PD, LGD and EAD for purchased corporate, etc. exposures using the top-down approach, estimates EL_{dilution}, or estimates PD, LGD, EAD and EL_{dilution} for purchased retail exposures, it shall satisfy all of the following requirements: (i) it satisfies the standards on the legal framework; (ii) it monitors the quality of the purchased receivables and the financial condition of the seller of the purchased receivables and of the servicer (meaning a person entrusted, under a mandate or sub-mandate, with the administration of the purchased receivables, the demand for payment of the purchased receivables from the obligors of the purchased receivables, and the receipt of collected funds; the same applies hereinafter in this Article), and satisfies the standards on monitoring; (iii) under the contract relating to the purchase of the purchased receivables, systems and procedures are in place that enable early detection of deterioration in the business condition of the seller or in the quality of the purchased receivables and preventive measures against possible problem situations, and it satisfies the standards on workout systems; (iv) clear and effective standards are established on collateral, the upper limit of credit extended by the creditor of the purchased receivables to the obligor, and the management of collected funds; (v) it satisfies the standards on compliance with all major policies and procedures within the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach.

Notwithstanding the preceding paragraph, for purchased retail exposures that satisfy the requirements set out in Article 159, Articles 161 through 163, Article 165, Article 171, Article 173, Article 174 and Article 176, for which the portion equivalent to dilution risk is judged to be immaterial, and to which the preceding Article does not apply, the requirements set out in items (iii) and (v) of the preceding paragraph need not be satisfied.

"The standards on the legal framework" in item (i) of paragraph (1) means the following: (i) that, in light of the structure of the transaction relating to the exposure, the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach has legally effective rights to principal and interest payments, etc. on the purchased receivables, and supervises such payments, in all foreseeable circumstances, including deterioration of the business condition of the seller or servicer of the purchased receivables, or their insolvency; (ii) that, where the obligors of the purchased receivables make payments directly to the seller or servicer of the purchased receivables, the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach regularly confirms that the payment funds are remitted from the seller or servicer to the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach as transferee in accordance with the contractual terms; (iii) that, in bankruptcy, corporate reorganization or civil rehabilitation proceedings of the seller of the purchased receivables, the court is considered not to determine that the purchased receivables belong to the bankruptcy estate, the reorganized company or the property of the seller subject to the civil rehabilitation proceedings, and not to determine that the transferee's rights in the purchased receivables are a security interest subject to bankruptcy, corporate reorganization or civil rehabilitation proceedings, and that the transfer of the purchased receivables is considered not subject to avoidance under the Bankruptcy Act (Act No. 75 of 2004), the Civil Rehabilitation Act (Act No. 225 of 1999) or the Corporate Reorganization Act (Act No. 154 of 2002), or to the right to rescind fraudulent acts under the Civil Code (Act No. 89 of 1896).

"The standards on monitoring" in item (ii) of paragraph (1) means the following: (i) that the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach assesses the correlation between the quality of the purchased receivables and the financial condition of the seller or servicer of the purchased receivables, and has in place contingency measures and procedures, such as the assignment of an obligor rating to the seller or servicer of the purchased receivables; (ii) that the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach has clear and effective policies and procedures for determining the eligibility of sellers and servicers of purchased receivables, and that the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach or its trustee regularly assesses the sellers and servicers, in order to verify the accuracy of reports sent by the seller or servicer of the purchased receivables, to investigate fraudulent acts and operational deficiencies, and to confirm the seller's credit extension standards and the servicer's collection policies and procedures, and records the results of such assessments in detail in writing; (iii) that the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach is able to evaluate the existence of credit extension exceeding the upper limit of credit to obligors set by the seller of the purchased receivables, delays in payment by the seller, the history of low-credit-quality receivables and unsound payment extensions, payment terms, amounts that may be set off, and other characteristics of the pool of purchased receivables; (iv) that the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach has effective policies and procedures to monitor concentration of credit extension to a single obligor on a gross basis in specific or all pools of purchased receivables; provided, however, that this does not apply to purchased retail exposures prescribed in paragraph (2); (v) that the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach receives in a timely manner from the servicer detailed reports on the deferment of obligations on the purchased receivables and on dilution of such receivables, confirms that the receivables conform to the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach's eligibility standards and credit extension standards for purchased receivables, and is able to monitor and confirm the seller's terms of sale and dilution.

"The standards on workout systems" in item (iii) of paragraph (1) means the following: (i) that the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach has clear and effective policies, procedures and information systems to monitor compliance with covenants, credit extension standards, limits on credit concentration, early amortization clauses, and other terms of the contract relating to the purchase of the purchased receivables, interest rates, and the policies within the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. that determine the eligibility of purchased receivables, and records covenant breaches and waivers and exceptional treatments of existing policies and procedures in that information system; (ii) that the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach has clear and effective policies, procedures and information systems for detecting, approving, monitoring and correcting excessive credit extension, in order to prevent inappropriate credit extension on purchased receivables; (iii) that the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach has established clear and effective policies and procedures on early termination clauses and other covenants in revolving transactions, responses to covenant breaches, commencement of legal proceedings and the treatment of exposures with deteriorated creditworthiness, and other matters, as well as clear and effective policies on the treatment of sellers or servicers of purchased receivables with a deteriorated financial condition or of a deterioration in the quality of a pool of purchased receivables.

"Clear and effective standards on collateral, the upper limit of credit extended by the creditor of the purchased receivables to the obligor, and the management of collected funds" in item (iv) of paragraph (1) means standards that satisfy all of the following characteristics: (i) all major matters relating to the purchase of receivables, such as interest rates, eligible collateral, required documents, limits on credit concentration and the treatment of collected funds, are specified in writing, and in specifying those major matters, the financial condition of the seller or servicer of the purchased receivables, concentration of risk, the quality of the purchased receivables, trends in the customer base of the seller, and all other relevant material factors have been taken into account; (ii) in internal management, the subjects of credit extension are limited to those accompanied by documents such as specified collateral, servicer certificates, invoice statements or bills-of-lading-related documents.

"The standards on compliance with all major policies and procedures within the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach" in item (v) of paragraph (1) means that effective internal procedures have been established to assess compliance with the following matters and all other major policies and procedures: (i) where the purchased receivables are purchased under a program, periodic internal or external assessments at all material stages of that program; (ii) confirmation that the personnel evaluating sellers and servicers of purchased receivables are separate and independent from the personnel evaluating obligors, and that the personnel conducting internal evaluations of sellers and servicers of purchased receivables are separate and independent from the personnel conducting external evaluations; (iii) evaluation of the back office (focusing on the qualifications and experience of personnel, the adequacy of staffing, and support systems).
